newsitem.title: USA: Court date set on appeal of Smith Corona plan.
newsitem.headline: Court date set on appeal of Smith Corona plan.

text.p: A hearing has been scheduled Monday on an appeal by Chase Manhattan Corp and BankAmerica Corp's Illinois unit of the court order approving Smith Corona Corp's reorganization plan for emerging from Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.

In papers filed in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, the banks, which provided Smith Corona Corp its debtor-in- possession financing, seek an expedited appeal of Tuesday's U.S. Bankruptcy Court order confirming the plan and an order staying implementation of the plan pending the appeal.

If a stay were granted, Smith Corona would have to postpone the anticipated February 8 effective date of the plan. That is also the date when stock in the reorganized company is expected to begin trading, possibly on NASDAQ.

At the confirmation hearing Tuesday, banks' attorney Joel Zweibel said a potential suit by unsecured creditors to recover the transfer of certain prepetition funds to the banks would cost more than the $650,000 in legal fees allotted the banks by the plan. The banks want any legal fees covered in full as administrative claims.
But chief bankruptcy judge in Delaware Helen Balick overruled the banks' objection, saying she would not allow the confirmation process to "be held hostage by the banks."
The appeal has been assigned to U.S. District Judge Roderick McKelvie.
